title: My Grandfather's Quiet Habit of Gratitude
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] My grandfather had a small habit that I only truly noticed after many, many years of watching him.
Narrator: [gently] Every single night, right before sleeping, he quietly said thanks for three simple, ordinary things.
Narrator: [curious] Sometimes it was just warm food on the table, or a car that started without trouble, or a short phone call from family.
Narrator: [reflective] I once asked him why he did this small habit so faithfully, every single night without exception.
Narrator: [warmly] He said, a grateful heart rarely stays angry for long, and it rarely stays truly empty either.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I asked if he ever skipped a night, maybe when he was too tired, or too upset about something.
Narrator: [gently] He smiled and said those were exactly the nights he needed the habit most, not the nights he could skip it.
Narrator: [honestly] I did not understand him fully back then. I thought gratitude was something you felt only during good times.
Narrator: [reflective] Years later, during a very difficult season of my own life, I remembered his words almost by accident.
Narrator: [with feeling] I tried it one night, forcing myself to name three small things despite feeling genuinely hopeless about everything else.
Narrator: [softly] It felt strange at first, almost forced, like I was pretending to feel something I clearly did not feel.
Narrator: [with wonder] But slowly, night after night, something shifted quietly inside me, even while my actual circumstances stayed exactly the same.
Narrator: [warmly] After he passed away, I started this same quiet habit myself, and I still continue it faithfully every single night now.
Narrator: [sincere] It's such a small, invisible thing, yet it has slowly changed how I see my whole ordinary day.
Narrator: [reflective] Nobody knows I do this. I've never mentioned it to my friends, and I never plan to, honestly.
Narrator: [peacefully] Righteousness, I have learned, often lives quietly inside these small, honest habits, far from anyone's attention or praise.

quiz.question: What did the narrator's grandfather do every night before sleeping?
options: He quietly said thanks for three simple things
quiz.explanation: Every night before sleeping, he quietly said thanks for three simple, ordinary things.

quiz.question: According to the grandfather, when did he need the habit most?
options: On tired or upset nights, not nights he could skip it
He didn't need it at all
quiz.explanation: He said the tired or upset nights were exactly the nights he needed the habit most.

quiz.question: When did the narrator finally try the habit herself?
options: Years later, during a very difficult season of her life
quiz.explanation: Years later, during a difficult season of her own life, she remembered his words and tried it.

quiz.question: How did the habit feel for the narrator at first?
options: Strange and forced, like pretending to feel something
quiz.explanation: She says it felt strange at first, almost forced, like pretending to feel something she didn't feel.

quiz.question: Has the narrator told her friends about this habit?
options: Yes, she talks about it often
No, and she never plans to
quiz.explanation: She says nobody knows she does this, she has never mentioned it to friends, and never plans to.
